title: Just as, bhikkhus, if someone in this Jeta's Grove were to take away, burn, or do whatever they wished with all the grass, sticks, branches,…
content: Just as, bhikkhus, if someone in this Jeta's Grove were to take away, burn, or do whatever they wished with all the grass, sticks, branches, and leaves, would you think: 'That person takes us away, burns us, or does whatever they wish with us'?" — "No, Venerable Sir." — "Why is that? Because that is not our self nor what belongs to our self. So too, bhikkhus, the eye is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness. Forms are not yours... Eye-consciousness is not yours... Eye-contact is not yours... Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact, whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that feeling is not yours, abandon it. Abandoning it will lead to your long-term welfare and happiness.

title: Brief is this life; within a hundred years, one dies. Even if one lives longer, one still dies of old age. People grieve for what…
content:
Brief is this life; within a hundred years, one dies.
Even if one lives longer, one still dies of old age.

People grieve for what they hold as 'mine';
All clinging is impermanent.
Seeing that this world is empty, one should live homeless.

People think: 'This is mine.'
But when they die, that is destroyed.
Knowing this, the wise person
Should not incline toward 'mine'.

Like a dream when one wakes up,
One sees nothing.
So too, what one holds dear and loved —
It dies, and one no longer sees it.

Thus, that person is seen and heard, called by this or that name.
But when one has died, only the name remains.

Greed for 'mine', they do not abandon.
Sorrow, lamentation, and stinginess.
Therefore, the seer, having abandoned grasping,
Lives a life of security.

title: Whatever beings are gathered together, Whether on the earth or in the sky, Let them worship the Buddha, the Tathāgata, Honored by devas and humans.…
content:
Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Buddha, the Tathāgata,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Dhamma, the Tathāgata's teaching,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

Whatever beings are gathered together,
Whether on the earth or in the sky,
Let them worship the Saṅgha, the Tathāgata's community,
Honored by devas and humans.
May there be happiness for all beings.

title: Therefore, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Bhikkhus, just…
content: Therefore, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline. Bhikkhus, just as near a village or town there is a great grove of tala trees, overgrown with castor-oil plants. A man comes who wants the grove's good, welfare, and security from bondage. He cuts down the crooked, withered branches and throws them out, cleans up the grove, and tends the straight, well-grown tala branches. After a time, that grove grows, prospers, and increases. So too, bhikkhus, abandon unwholesome states and strive for wholesome states. Thus you will achieve growth, prosperity, and increase in this Dhamma and Discipline.

title: One who delights in the eye, bhikkhus, delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights…
content: One who delights in the eye, bhikkhus, delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the ear ... in the nose ... One who delights in the tongue, bhikkhus, delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in the body ... One who delights in the mind, delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. And one who does not delight in the eye, bhikkhus, does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the ear ... in the nose ... One who does not delight in the tongue, does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in the body ... One who does not delight in the mind, does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.

title: Venerable Mettagū: What you have asked us, you have answered. Now I ask another question; please explain it to me: How do the wise cross…
content:
Venerable Mettagū:
What you have asked us, you have answered.
Now I ask another question; please explain it to me:
How do the wise cross the strong flood,
Cross birth and old age, lamentation and sorrow?
May the seer answer me well,
As you have known the Dhamma-nature.

The Blessed One:
I will tell you the Dhamma directly seen,
Not handed down. Having known it,
Living mindfully, one overcomes attachment to the world.

Whatever you know above, below, across, and in between,
Abandon delight and dwelling,
Do not let consciousness settle on existence.

Living thus, mindful, a bhikkhu not heedless,
Having abandoned deeds leading to 'I' and 'mine',
Here, knowing birth and old age, lamentation and sorrow,
Abandon suffering.

That brahmin who has directly known and is wise,
Having nothing, not attached to existence,
Certainly crosses this flood,
Has gone to the far shore, without stiffness, without hesitation.

Having known and understood the sacred teaching,
Not caught in this attachment to existence or non-existence,
Free from craving, without distress, without longing —
Him I say has crossed birth and old age.

title: Bhikkhus, these eight things lead to the non-decline of a learner bhikkhu. What eight? Not delighting in work, not delighting in talking, not delighting in…
content: Bhikkhus, these eight things lead to the non-decline of a learner bhikkhu. What eight? Not delighting in work, not delighting in talking, not delighting in sleeping, not delighting in company, sense restraint, moderation in eating, not delighting in association, not delighting in frivolous talk. Bhikkhus, these eight things lead to the non-decline of a learner bhikkhu.

title: The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, cross-legged, holding his body straight, contemplating his own peace. Then the Blessed One, having…
content:
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, cross-legged, holding his body straight, contemplating his own peace. Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

A bhikkhu with peaceful mind,
Has cut the cord of birth and death.
The wandering in birth and death is ended,
Freed from Māra's bonds.

title: - Just as, bhikkhus, a person throws a yoke with a single hole into the great ocean. There is a blind turtle that surfaces once…
content: - Just as, bhikkhus, a person throws a yoke with a single hole into the great ocean. There is a blind turtle that surfaces once every hundred years. What do you think, bhikkhus, would that blind turtle, surfacing once every hundred years, put its neck into that yoke with a single hole?" - "It might, Venerable Sir, after a very long time." - "I say, bhikkhus, that the blind turtle surfacing once every hundred years would put its neck into that yoke with a single hole more quickly than a fool who has fallen into a plane of misery could regain human birth. Why is that? Because there, bhikkhus, there is no practice of Dhamma, no righteous conduct, no wholesome deeds, no meritorious deeds. There, bhikkhus, they devour one another, and the weak are eaten. Why is that? Because they do not see the Four Noble Truths. What four? The Noble Truth of Suffering ... the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

title: There are these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus. What two? Giving of material goods and giving of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of…
content: There are these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus. What two? Giving of material goods and giving of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of giving. The foremost among these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus, is the giving of the Dhamma. There are these two kinds of offerings, bhikkhus. What two? Offering of material goods and offering of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of offerings. The foremost among these two kinds of offerings, bhikkhus, is the offering of the Dhamma. There are these two kinds of wealth, bhikkhus. What two? Material wealth and Dhamma wealth. These are the two kinds of wealth. The foremost among these two kinds of wealth, bhikkhus, is Dhamma wealth.
